passage: Many plants respond to insect attacks by increasing their production of defensive compounds, but the cues that alert a plant to an attack are not fully understood. Chemical ecologist Heidi Appel and biologist Rex Cocroft tested whether vibrations might be one such cue. Using actuators attached to the leaves of thale cress (Arabidopsis thaliana), they played back recordings of the vibrations that caterpillars produce while chewing. When caterpillars later fed on these plants, the plants produced more chemical defenses than did plants kept in silence. Vibrations from wind or from a harmless insect’s mating call elicited no comparable response.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: It describes research indicating that plants can respond to the vibrations produced by feeding insects.
It explains how caterpillars use vibrations in leaves to find plants with weak chemical defenses.
It discusses a debate about whether laboratory studies of plants reflect what happens in the wild.
It presents findings showing that caterpillars eat less of plants that have been exposed to recorded vibrations.

passage: Early in her career, ceramicist Toshiko Takaezu (1922–2011) produced utilitarian wares such as teapots, plates, and bottles. In the late 1950s, however, she came to regard ceramics as artworks meant to be contemplated rather than used, and she subsequently sealed the openings of her vessels, creating hollow sculptures known as closed forms. Before sealing a form, Takaezu often inserted a fragment of clay wrapped in paper; during firing, the paper burned away, leaving a concealed rattle. Takaezu considered the most important aspect of these works to be their interiors, “the dark space that you can’t see.”
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To trace how Takaezu’s glazes changed after she moved from Hawaii to the mainland
To characterize a kind of ceramic work Takaezu developed and what she valued in it
To argue that Takaezu’s closed forms should be classified as sculpture rather than pottery
To explain how Takaezu designed her rattles to be heard by visitors to her exhibitions

passage: Elephants that leave Kenya’s Tsavo East National Park to raid nearby farms threaten the livelihoods of small-scale farmers. Because elephants avoid bees, Lucy King of the conservation organization Save the Elephants and her collaborators tested an unconventional barrier. From 2012 to 2015, beehives were suspended every 10 meters along the boundaries of farm plots near the park, linked by wire so that an elephant pushing through would set them swinging. Roughly 80 percent of the elephants that approached the fenced farms turned away, and selling the honey gave farmers an additional source of income.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To trace the causes of growing conflict between elephants and farmers in Kenya
To suggest that beehive fences could protect crops from a wide range of wild animals
To present a method of keeping elephants off farms and the results of testing it
To describe how farmers near the park learned to keep bees and sell honey

passage: Efforts to protect pollinating insects tend to focus on bees, while hoverflies, which resemble small bees or wasps, have received far less attention. That imbalance is hard to justify. In a 2019 study based on radar data, a team including Karl Wotton and Jason Chapman estimated that up to four billion hoverflies migrate over southern Britain each year, carrying billions of pollen grains between Britain and continental Europe. Many hoverflies are also valuable before they can fly: their larvae feed on aphids, crop pests that locally produced hoverflies consume by the trillions annually.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To describe the radar technology used to track insects that migrate at high altitudes
To compare how effectively hoverflies and bees pollinate crops
To warn that hoverfly populations in Britain have declined in recent years
To argue that hoverflies deserve more attention for the benefits they provide

passage: Between 1875 and 1878, Cheyenne and Kiowa men imprisoned at Fort Marion in Florida produced hundreds of drawings in paper books, many of them sold to tourists as souvenirs. Art historian Joyce M. Szabo has shown, however, that some of these books resulted from more complicated arrangements between artist and patron. <u>In 1877, for instance, Eva Scott Fényes, who taught English to several of the prisoners, commissioned books from the Kiowa artist Zotom and the Cheyenne artist Howling Wolf.</u> Szabo concludes that Fényes largely determined the subjects of Zotom’s drawings, whereas Howling Wolf preferred to choose his own.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

passage: Many online services appear to operate entirely through automated software. Behind them, however, people paid by the task often perform work that algorithms cannot yet handle reliably, from flagging objectionable images to captioning videos and proofreading text. <u>Anthropologist Mary L. Gray and computer scientist Siddharth Suri call this largely invisible labor “ghost work.”</u> Drawing on a five-year study of workers in the United States and India, Gray and Suri report in their 2019 book that people who do ghost work typically receive no health benefits and can be dismissed at any time, for any reason or none.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?

It supplies a name for the labor described in the previous sentence.

passage: Many theories of language development treat speech that caregivers address directly to children as a principal driver of language learning. <u>Those theories have been shaped largely by studies of middle-class families in Western countries.</u> To examine children’s language environments elsewhere, Marisa Casillas, Penelope Brown, and Stephen C. Levinson analyzed daylong audio recordings of ten children, aged two months to three years, in a Tseltal Mayan village in southern Mexico. The children were rarely spoken to directly, yet indicators such as the timing of babbling and first words suggested that their language development was proceeding successfully.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence?
options: It describes the methods typically used in studies of Western families.
It notes a limitation of the evidence behind the theories mentioned in the previous sentence.
It summarizes the results of the study conducted in the Tseltal Mayan village.

passage: Sea otters, the smallest marine mammals, lack the insulating blubber of whales and seals, and their dense fur alone cannot keep them warm in cold water. Instead, their basal metabolic rate is roughly three times that predicted for a mammal of their size. But which tissues generate the additional heat? <u>A 2021 study by Traver Wright, a physiologist at Texas A&M University, and his team pointed to skeletal muscle.</u> Muscle samples from otters of various ages showed exceptionally high leak respiration, a process in which muscles consume energy without performing mechanical work, releasing it as heat.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It reports a finding that answers the question raised in the preceding sentence.
It describes how the researchers obtained muscle samples from otters of various ages.
It introduces a hypothesis that the evidence in the following sentence calls into question.
It suggests that blubber matters less to marine mammals than scientists once believed.

passage: Frogs reproduce in a remarkable variety of ways, yet in nearly all species, eggs are fertilized outside the female’s body. As of 2014, <u>fewer than a dozen of the 6,455 recognized frog species were known to fertilize eggs internally, and each of those either laid fertilized eggs or gave birth to froglets</u>. That year, however, zoologist Djoko Iskandar of Indonesia’s Bandung Institute of Technology and two coauthors described the fanged frog Limnonectes larvaepartus, found only on the island of Sulawesi, whose females give birth to live tadpoles and deposit them in slow-moving streams or small pools.
stem: Which choice best states the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?
options: It describes how researchers determined the number of frog species that fertilize eggs internally.
It presents a hypothesis about frog reproduction that the discovery of Limnonectes larvaepartus confirmed.
It summarizes the reproductive patterns that Limnonectes larvaepartus was found to depart from.
It accounts for the rarity of internal fertilization among frogs.

passage: By the 1960s, the last native speakers of myaamia, the language of the Miami people, had died, a loss accelerated by the nation’s forced removal from its Great Lakes homeland. Beginning in the early 1990s, Daryl Baldwin, a citizen of the Miami Tribe of Oklahoma, nevertheless taught himself the language, relying on linguist David Costa’s analyses of archival documents that included dictionaries compiled by French missionaries. Baldwin subsequently earned a master’s degree in linguistics, taught myaamia to his family, and in 2001 became founding director of the Myaamia Project at Miami University in Ohio, now a center that develops educational materials with the tribe.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall purpose of the text?
options: To explain why the Miami people were forced to leave their homeland in the Great Lakes region
To compare the methods Baldwin and Costa used to study historical records of myaamia
To show that myaamia has again become the primary language of the Miami Tribe of Oklahoma
To describe Baldwin’s role in reviving a language that had lost its last native speakers

passage: Because details tend to shift each time a story is retold, oral traditions are often dismissed as unreliable records of the distant past. A 2016 study by geographer Patrick Nunn and linguist Nicholas Reid suggests that such skepticism can go too far. Nunn and Reid examined Aboriginal Australian stories from 21 coastal sites, each describing land that is now under the sea, and compared the water depth each account implies with the established record of sea-level rise after the last ice age. By that measure, the stories preserve observations made more than 7,000 years ago. Oral traditions deserve serious consideration as historical evidence.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To argue that oral traditions can be valuable sources of information about the distant past
To explain how rising seas altered the way of life of Aboriginal Australians
To question the accuracy of the sea-level record that Nunn and Reid relied on
To show that oral traditions are generally more dependable than written records

The following text is adapted from Jessie Redmon Fauset’s 1924 novel There Is Confusion. Joanna Marshall, a dancer, has become a star on Broadway.

[Joanna] was beginning to feel the need of something with which to fill her life. But life, she began to realize, was not a matter of sufficient raiment, food, or even success. There must be something more filling, more insistent, more permeating—the sort of thing that left no room for boredom or introspection. For in spite of her vogue, her unbelievably decided successes, Joanna frequently tasted the depths of ennui. She saw life as a ghastly skeleton and herself feverishly trying to cover up its bare bones with the garish trappings of her art, her lessons, her practice, her press-clippings.

options: To portray Joanna’s satisfaction with the recognition that her art has finally earned
To convey Joanna’s sense that her stage triumphs have not filled an emptiness in her life
To suggest that Joanna’s fame has made her impatient with the admirers who seek her company
To illustrate how the strain of constant performing has begun to damage Joanna’s health

passage: Radiocarbon dating of charcoal preserved in the sediments of an ancient channel led archaeologist Ian McNiven and colleagues to conclude that the Gunditjmara people of what is now southeastern Australia were already manipulating the waterways around the volcano Budj Bim at least 6,600 years ago. Drawing on the abundant volcanic rock of the area’s lava flows, the Gunditjmara <u>built channels, weirs, and dams that controlled the flow of water, enabling them to trap, store, and harvest kooyang, or short-finned eels</u>. UNESCO describes the network as one of the world’s oldest and most extensive aquaculture systems.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?
options: It explains how the archaeologists determined the age of the channel mentioned in the previous sentence.
It describes a later change in how the Gunditjmara lived that UNESCO regards as more significant than the system’s age.
It details the structures that the final sentence identifies as an early and extensive form of aquaculture.
It qualifies the previous sentence’s claim about when the Gunditjmara began to manipulate the waterways.

passage: <u>Many trees reproduce by mast seeding, or masting: individuals across a population synchronously produce enormous seed crops in some years and very few in others.</u> Bumper years satiate seed predators, allowing many seeds to escape consumption. Analyzing nearly four decades of seed production by European beech trees in England, ecologist Michał Bogdziewicz and colleagues found that as the climate warmed, the trees produced more seed overall but varied less from year to year and less in unison, while losses to seed-eating moth larvae climbed. The main beneficiaries of the trees’ increased seed production, the researchers conclude, are not the trees but their predators.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the first sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a hypothesis about seed predators that Bogdziewicz and colleagues set out to test.
It defines a reproductive pattern whose disruption the text goes on to describe.
It describes a recent change in beech trees’ behavior that the researchers attribute to rising temperatures.
It explains why moth larvae have destroyed a growing share of beech seeds in England.

passage: Metamaterials, structures whose unusual physical properties arise from the arrangement of many tiny elements rather than from the materials they are made of, are rare in nature, and until recently no acoustic example was known. Biologist Thomas Neil and colleagues have found that the scale layer on moths’ wings is one: <u>each scale acts as a resonator tuned to a specific frequency, and because the scales are coupled through the wing membrane, together they absorb ultrasound across the full range of frequencies that bats use in echolocation</u>. This acoustic camouflage is achieved with a layer thin and light enough for flight.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?
options: It describes the procedure the researchers followed to measure how much ultrasound moth wings absorb.
It qualifies the previous sentence’s claim that acoustic metamaterials are rare in nature.
It explains why bats have been unable to adjust their calls to detect moths in flight.
It explains how moths’ wing scales function together as an acoustic metamaterial.

A girl in an orange-coloured shawl stood at the window of Pedlar’s store and looked, through the falling snow, at the deserted road. Though she watched there without moving, her attitude, in its stillness, gave an impression of <u>arrested flight, as if she were running toward life</u>.

passage: Because avian mothers cannot modify their embryos’ biochemical environment after laying, it has been unclear whether birds can prepare their offspring for prevailing climatic conditions. Ecologists Mylene Mariette and Katherine Buchanan found that incubating zebra finches emit a distinctive call to their eggs late in incubation, and only when temperatures exceed 26°C. Embryos exposed to recordings of this call gained less mass in hotter nests as nestlings, a pattern the researchers linked to greater reproductive success, and as adults they consistently bred in hotter nest boxes than individuals that had heard a different call.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: It discusses research suggesting that zebra finch embryos alert their parents when the temperature inside the egg rises too high.
It describes a study indicating that some birds may prepare their offspring for hot conditions by signaling to them before they hatch.
It presents evidence that the heat zebra finch embryos experience inside the egg determines how much they will grow after hatching.
It explains why zebra finches have bred more successfully than other songbirds as temperatures in their habitats have risen.

passage: In 2016, while her brother, the reindeer herder Jovsset Ánte Sara, was contesting a state-mandated cull that he argued would render his livelihood economically unviable, Sámi artist Máret Ánne Sara heaped 200 reindeer heads from a slaughterhouse outside the courthouse in Tana Bru, Norway, and planted a Norwegian flag on top. That intervention inaugurated Pile o’Sápmi, an ongoing project whose subsequent works include a flag fashioned from hundreds of bullet-pierced reindeer skulls. Exhibited alongside an 1892 photograph of a mound of bison skulls, the project places the cull within a longer history of colonial violence.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To explain why the Norwegian state ordered reductions in Sámi reindeer herds and how herders contested those orders in court
To argue that Pile o’Sápmi has proved more effective as a form of political protest than as a work of art
To show how an artist’s protest on her brother’s behalf became a project that sets a present-day dispute in historical perspective
To compare the culling of reindeer in Norway with the killing of bison in North America in order to identify their shared causes

passage: The Silk Road is popularly imagined as a highway along which merchant caravans conveyed silk and other luxuries in great volume between China and Rome. But the contracts and other everyday documents preserved in the dry sands of the Taklamakan Desert led historian Valerie Hansen to a far more modest picture: direct commerce between China and Rome was minimal, and most exchange consisted of small-scale transactions among local peddlers. What principally sustained the region’s economy, Hansen contends, was government expenditure, notably the bolts of silk with which the Tang dynasty paid the garrisons stationed on its northwestern frontier.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To present a historian’s reassessment, drawn from everyday records, of the scale and nature of Silk Road commerce
To argue that the Tang dynasty’s spending on its frontier garrisons ultimately disrupted the trade between China and Rome
To describe how documents found in the Taklamakan Desert reveal the routes that caravans followed between China and Rome
To explain how local peddlers distributed the silk that the Tang dynasty used to pay the soldiers on its frontier

passage: For much of the twentieth century, scholars of Hawai‘i relied on a small canon of nineteenth-century Hawaiian writings that had been translated into English. M. stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

passage: Rock varnish is a dark coating that forms on exposed rock surfaces in deserts worldwide. <u>Its most perplexing feature is its composition: varnish typically contains two to three orders of magnitude more manganese than the underlying rock or the surrounding dust from which much of its mass derives.</u> Analyzing varnish from the western United States, geobiologist Usha Lingappa and colleagues found it rich in cyanobacteria of the genus Chroococcidiopsis. These microbes stockpile manganese inside their cells, apparently using the metal as an antioxidant. Such uptake by the coating’s pioneer microbes, the researchers propose, accounts for its enrichment.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It identifies a puzzling property of a material that the research described in the rest of the text helps account for.

It explains why rock varnish forms only on the exposed rock surfaces of the deserts mentioned in the previous sentence.
